page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-96 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor. It features 96 vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with multithreading enabled, delivering a dedicated CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 384 GB of RAM, establishing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU. It operates on the x86_64 architecture and includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including VNNI and BF16 variants, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data places this instance in the top tier for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 165,169.51 and a PassMark CPU score of 115,229.69. Memory subsystem performance is strong, registering a cached read-only small block bandwidth of 9,925.2 GB/sec and uncached large block read and write speeds of 283.29 GB/sec and 164.6 GB/sec respectively. Database operations and memory-bound tasks perform efficiently, as demonstrated by a PassMark database score of 40,029.74 and Redis SET throughput reaching 161.14 million operations per second.

The instance is suited for multi-threaded computational workloads, web serving, and database operations, supported by a static web serving throughput of 93.11 GB/sec. It also handles small-to-medium language model inference, achieving 345.24 tokens per second for text generation on a 135M parameter model and 55.64 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware limits its applicability for workloads requiring high-speed local disk I/O or heavy parallel graphics processing. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high resource density of 96 dedicated vCPUs combined with top-tier CPU and memory bandwidth benchmarks provides a consolidated platform for virtualization and enterprise-scale applications without the overhead of specialized hardware.
description: The Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-96 is an x86_64 general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs (48 physical cores) and 384 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. The processor supports advanced vector and cryptographic instructions, including AVX-512 and AES. In benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates top-tier CPU and memory performance, achieving a stress-ng multi-core score of 165,169.51 and a Redis throughput of 161.14 million operations per second. While it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, its high memory bandwidth and processing capacity make it highly efficient for multi-threaded enterprise applications, database operations, static web serving, and small-to-medium language model inference.
